concerns.advisory: The change to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` in server-spi alters behavior for every caller of that shared predicate, not just the new login cache — org-linked IDPs without `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` are now filtered out everywhere the predicate is used (including JPA/map store `getForLogin` implementations and any extension that calls it).
concerns.why: server-spi/.../IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java: `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` added to the public static `getLoginPredicate()`.

concerns.advisory: `getForLogin` now returns models resolved via `session.identityProviders().getById(...)` and wrapped as organization-aware, which can flip `isEnabled()`, so the returned stream no longer satisfies the login predicate it was cached under — callers must re-filter, and only the freemarker bean was updated to do so.
concerns.why: OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean adds `idp.isEnabled() &&` with the comment "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped", while other consumers of `getForLogin` are unchanged.

concerns.advisory: The login cache key is per (realm, FetchMode) but a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` holds per-organization result sets, so querying a not-yet-cached organization invalidates and rebuilds the whole shared entry — in realms with many organizations this can thrash the cache and repeatedly re-hit the DB.
concerns.why: `getForLogin`: `if (cached == null) { cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey); ... new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query); }` under `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` which excludes organizationId.

concerns.advisory: Any create/remove/update of a login-qualifying IDP invalidates the login caches for all FetchModes and therefore for every organization in the realm, so a single org's IDP change discards cached login lists for all other orgs.
concerns.why: `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` / `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` loop `for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values())` and invalidate `cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)` unconditionally.

concerns.advisory: `remove(alias)` now performs an unconditional `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` delegate/DB lookup on every removal, including the previously cache-served path that avoided it.
concerns.why: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` was hoisted above the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch.

concerns.advisory: `create()` invalidates the login caches for all FetchModes before delegating, using a model that cannot yet have an organization link, so newly created realm-level IDPs needlessly discard the ORG_ONLY cached lists.

When a cached internal ID no longer resolves to an IDP, the code silently invalidates and falls back to the delegate with no logging or metric, so a persistently stale login cache degrades into full DB reads on every login page render without any signal.

During a rolling upgrade, old nodes use the pre-change login predicate and will not register login-cache invalidations for org-linked non-public IDPs that new nodes consider cache-relevant, so new nodes can serve stale login IDP lists until restart.
concerns.why: Invalidation decisions in `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` depend on the newly redefined `getLoginPredicate()`, while cluster invalidation events are produced by whichever node handles the write.

concerns.advisory: The new test's cleanup registers removal of a hard-coded alias `"alias"` rather than the aliases actually created, so the ~21 IDPs and org links created by this test are never cleaned up and may leak into other tests in the class.
concerns.why: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` appears twice while the created aliases are `idp-alias-<i>`.

concerns.advisory: The new test never covers removing or creating an IDP that *is* available for login, so the invalidation paths in `create()` and `remove()` (as opposed to `update()`) are unverified.
concerns.why: Step 1 only removes `idp-alias-1` (disabled, non-login) and creates a `hideOnLogin=true` IDP, then asserts caches are *not* invalidated; steps 3 and 4 exercise only `update`.

concerns.advisory: The test asserts cache state only within a single node/session and does not exercise cross-node invalidation, leaving the clustered behavior of the new `.idp.login` cache keys unverified.
concerns.why: All assertions run inside `getTestingClient().server(TEST_REALM_NAME).run(...)` against a single `RealmCacheSession`.

concerns.advisory: The javadoc on `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` documents non-invalidation conditions but omits that the login-qualification check itself depends on the `BROKER_PUBLIC` config flag, so a maintainer reading it may not realize toggling that config on an org-linked IDP is what drives invalidation.
concerns.why: The javadoc lists only "login IDP" status and organization link, while `getLoginPredicate()` was extended with the `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC` condition in the same PR.
